regions.summary: Exact byte-transition boundaries and current code conflicts were checked in the phase-one review. This supports generic non-code storage only; padding, decoded graphics and original generator remain unproven. Uniform $FF non-code byte run; specific use/fill purpose unresolved.

editorial_audit.notes: Final editorial assessment reuses verified reviews of all 1159 physical regions and 797 meaningful units; no pending entries. Reconciled four user-directed Data intervals (9 bytes, Manual confidence 0, original role UNKNOWN). Fixed stale structural-Unknown prose for accepted continuations/button masks/bounce profiles and removed duplicate bounce-profile include; preserved bank contexts, aliases, hypotheses and meaningful unit records. Source locations refreshed and embedded unit dictionaries reconcile audit API. Generic asset purposes, natural selector coverage, standalone callers and genuine ending remain unresolved; no hardware compatibility claim. See analysis/final-audit/editorial-findings.md. Audit preflight additionally exposed one reviewed scrolling continuation without a unit reference; inspected preceding dirty-flag test and tail jump and added its meaningful unit record (798 unique units total).

units.name: ResetVector
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 512..515 Reset jumps to the interrupt-disabled machine initialization entry.

units.name: FrameInterruptVector
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 568..571 IM1 jumps to the frame interrupt handler. The handler itself is reviewed separately.

units.name: PauseNmi
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 614..656 Pause NMI preserves AF. Only session flag pattern 04 permits a toggle; a 15-frame debounce prevents immediate retriggering. Toggle the pause latch and clear its debounce counter.

units.name: MachineInitialize
units.summary: Initialize stack and IM1, then map ROM bank 6 into the 8000 window.

units.name: DispatchMainMode
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 775..800 Service the frame synchronization helper, then dispatch through nine little-endian CPU words. Push this entry as the handler return address; the low mode nibble selects an unchecked word. The observed mode contract keeps the index within the table; this fragment does not enforce it.

units.name: PollModeButtons
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 818..824 Mode bit 7 enables this input path. Preserve a return continuation on the stack, sample controller state and recognize newly changed action-button bits 30. Mode 41 becomes 03; other eligible modes enter 86. The last-button latch suppresses repeats. Calls and raw gaps remain separate physical source ranges.

units.name: AdvanceInputSequence
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 935..979 Only advance an enabled, unfinished input sequence when controller state changes to nonzero. Alternate registers preserve the caller state while the sequence counter selects one of six masks. A matching masked input sets the completion flag; the precise sequence purpose is unresolved.

units.name: EnterModeOnce
units.summary: Mode bit 6 is the one-time initialization latch. Already initialized execution branches to CPU 0305; the intervening initialization path is retained in source order.

units.name: SelectModeSubstep
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1285..1304 Read the next state byte: substeps 1 and 2 branch to separate handlers. Other values initialize a 0600 word in the C70C work area and call the update helper.

units.name: TickModeCounter
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1331..1335 Decrement the C63F mode counter. Its surrounding handler is not fully classified.

units.name: CompleteModeTransition
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1405..1415 Return while the high bit of AttractSequenceFlags remains set; otherwise enter mode 82.

units.name: UpdateAttractPages
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1449..1460 Only active sequences run. Select ROM bank 9, then test the page-animation flag. A 24-tick timer alternates two destination addresses for a 34-byte update. A separate 180-tick timer advances through three page destinations using a word table. The last page clears the active flag. The visual meaning of each page is unresolved.

units.name: EnableAttractPageAnimation
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1538..1540 Set bit 6 in the caller-selected flag byte; its predecessor bytes remain unclassified.

units.name: InitializeStageSelector
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1834..1883 Initialize this mode once; clear C028-DDFF while retaining the mode/input header. Reset stage selection to zero. Session input-sequence flags choose the alternate selector path. ROM bank 5 is selected for the following presentation transfer.

units.name: UpdateStageSelector
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1883..1977 Copy the selector presentation, then poll at a one-tick cadence and suppress held inputs. Direction bit 0 decrements with wrap from 0 to 18; the other direction increments modulo 19. Each choice addresses a 16-byte presentation row at BE00 + index*16 in ROM bank 5. An action button takes a continuation beyond this classified fragment.

units.name: InitializeModeEight
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 1982..1986 Disable interrupts for display setup, select bank 2 and unpack the fixed stream at CPU 8395 to VRAM 2160. Enter mode 8 and reset several work counters. The game meanings of C07A/C044/C0A6-C0A8/C06C-C06D remain unresolved.

units.name: UpdateGameplay
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2040..2063 Session bits 0 and 1 divert to death/clear-like continuations. Otherwise run the frame object/display helpers, select bank 2 and call its ADAF helper. Decrement GameplayCountdown only when nonzero. Calls alone do not establish hidden helper semantics.

units.name: RequestGameplayTransition86
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 2081..2091 Write request 86 to DE03 and clear work flag C07C bit 6. The request consumer needs further review before assigning a game-specific name.

units.name: RequestGameplayTransition88
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 2142..2169 Write request 88. C652 bit 2 selects an alternate presentation that hides the sprite list with the D0 terminator and sets work byte C614. Clear C07C bit 6 in either case.

units.name: BeginStageClear
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2182..2185 Wait through frame synchronization until the condition helper returns zero. Issue helper request 9, clear nine stage-progress bytes C093-C09B and clear session bit 1. Session bit 7 selects an alternate continuation. Artificial clear experiments confirm this path, not natural victory or an ending.

units.name: AdvanceStageAfterClear
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2277..2280 C652 bit 2 selects an object-completion wait before advancing the stage. Increment StageIndex; choose mode 8 while the result is at most 18, otherwise mode 7. Restore the C06C counter from C06D on the alternate path and tail-call the shared reset helper.

units.name: InitializeStageGraphics
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2335..2395 Clear the C100-D7FF work area and prepare display state with interrupts disabled. Unpack fixed four-plane RLE assets from bank 2 to VRAM 2000 and 2160, then bank 4 CPU 9780 to VRAM 02C0. Each consumer advances its source to the stream terminator.

units.name: LoadSelectedStageGraphics
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2407..2412 In bank 15, index B2B7 by StageIndex*3. Each record is one effective ROM bank followed by a little-endian stream pointer. Select that bank and unpack to VRAM 2800. The descriptor domain is 19 records; stream validation established four equal output planes.

units.name: InitializeStagePresentation
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2443..2446 Run stage support initializers, then initialize scroll/control work bytes and terminate the sprite-Y list with D0. Re-enable interrupts. In bank 2, select a stage word from CPU 86B0 into C0A4, then switch to bank 9 for object parameters.

units.name: LoadStageObjectParameters
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2518..2598 In ROM bank 9, stage-indexed word tables initialize primary-object bytes C1C3/C1C6 and C09C. A byte selector chooses one of four-byte parameter records copied to C09E-C0A1. C652 bit 2 chooses request 87 instead of 81; precise request semantics remain unresolved.

units.name: QueueStageResource
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2600..2631 Store the selected request in DE03. In ROM bank 9, a stage word from AAF0 yields a resource pointer; skip its first byte and submit it with bank value 9.

units.name: CommitStageInitialization
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2631..2645 Set session bit 2. If bit 3 is clear, enter gameplay mode 4; otherwise preserve the caller-selected main mode. This is the supported artificial-stage initialization contract.

units.name: InitializeStageScroll
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2670..2675 Select ROM bank 9 and copy seven bytes from an eight-byte stage record into C64C-C652. Select bank 15, initialize the source/destination work pointers and scroll state. Stage 14 uses the special coordinate setup below.

units.name: InitializeStageFourteenScroll
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 2733..2768 For stage 14, use the alternate C928 work destination and establish the special coordinate words and mode byte before joining ordinary stage-parameter setup.

units.name: LoadStageScrollParameters
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2768..2798 Index bank-15 table B2F0 by StageIndex*2, then copy sixteen parameter bytes into C71C-C72B. C700 bit 4 chooses the coordinate conversion below.

units.name: ConvertReverseScrollCoordinate
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 2798..2826 Negate the low coordinate byte to extract its tile-phase bit. Add the C719 and C71B words with carry into C71D, then retain the upper coordinate bytes.

units.name: ConvertForwardScrollCoordinate
units.summary: Extract bit 3 into C708, divide the C71C coordinate by sixteen and store its low result in C709, then jump into the shared coordinate continuation.

units.name: SelectStageScrollPair
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2915..2920 In ROM bank 9, choose a stage pointer from AA72. A four-byte subrecord indexed by C71E supplies two little-endian words copied to C728 and C72A.

units.name: LoadStageSpriteResources
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 2960..2965 In bank 15, copy a 78-byte stage sprite-resource list into RAM D520. Its first byte counts entries. Each entry selects an effective bank, an RLE source word and a VRAM destination word. A following optional count/pointer requests a bit-reversed VRAM copy. This is the consumer behind the independently validated counted lists.

units.name: NormalizeStageProgressSlots
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3040..3054 Scan nine stage-progress bytes. Zero slots are skipped; nonzero slots retain only bits 4F. The precise progression meaning of those bits is still unresolved.

units.name: LoadStageProgressSlots
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3062..3067 Select bank 9, read the stage word from AE6E and copy nine bytes into StageProgressSlots. These are the slots cleared and normalized by the stage-clear path.

units.name: InitializeTerminalMode
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3099..3102 Mode bit 6 prevents repeated initialization. Disable interrupts, set VDP register 0, clear C100-DDFF and prepare the fixed bank-2 graphics. Apply the presentation descriptor at CPU 0A86, set a 300-tick condition counter and queue the palette at 0A9D. This artificial route was observed at GAME OVER; a genuine ending remains unproven.

units.name: PollTerminalExit
units.summary: Either controller action button can finish this screen. Otherwise decrement the 16-bit condition counter and return until it reaches zero. Clear the button latch before the exit setup and deferred mode selection.

units.name: InitializeBriefingMode
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3233..3246 Set session bit 2 and initialize this mode only once. Clear sprite/object working memory, seed the primary object and animation-table pointers, then select a stage presentation rectangle. The duplicated pointer writes are original behavior. Bank selections are explicit; the initial bank-2 pointer table must be read before switching.

units.name: FinishBriefingAndStartStage
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 3353..3362 Load the bank-5 RLE presentation, then use the stage palette word. The later path waits for PrimaryObjectFlags to clear, enters stage-initialization mode 5 and submits the same stage palette through the transition helper.

units.name: WaitForFrame
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3540..3559 Clear the frame-completion byte, service the pause helper if paused, then wait until the interrupt increments it. The pause loop re-enters at the pause test.

units.name: ClearDisplayTables
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3589..3613 Fill 0380 words at VRAM 3800 with the word stored at CPU 0C02, then fill 64 bytes at VRAM 3F00 with the byte at CPU 0C04. These are name/sprite-table resets.

units.name: DecrementConditionCounter
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3613..3616 Decrement the C615 16-bit counter and return Z when it reaches zero. There is no saturation: callers must stop decrementing after completion.

units.name: ApplyTransferList
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3623..3644 HL points to a count followed by transfer records: destination word, byte count word and that many inline bytes. Transfer each payload to VRAM and advance over it.

units.name: MultiplyUnsignedBytes
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3644..3656 Multiply the initial H byte by E using eight shift/add steps; return the unsigned 16-bit product in HL. D is cleared before the accumulator loop.

units.name: SampleGameplayController
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3703..3723 Session bit 2 enables sampling. Bit 4 selects another input route outside this classified fragment; ordinary sampling preserves the previous state before reading controller 1.

units.name: ReadControllerOne
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3734..3740 Return active-high six-button controller-1 bits by inverting port DC and masking 3F.

units.name: ReadControllerTwo
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3740..3742 Combine controller-2 bits split across DC and DD, invert to active-high and return six button/direction bits. RL C supplies the two DC bits to RLA.

units.name: SelectBankFourInputContinuation
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 3755..3760 Select bank 4. The following input continuation has not been classified.

units.name: FrameInterruptHandler
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3862..3900 Read VDP status; non-frame interrupts branch to a separate fragment. Save both register sets, index registers and the current 8000-window bank. Sample console reset on DD bit 4 and detect a falling edge using the previous sample. Bank 6 serves that path.

units.name: SelectFrameUpload
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3911..3924 VDP data port is BE. Upload-control C614 bits 7 and 6 choose the display update route. When both request it, C63B supplies the ROM bank for the queued pattern upload.

units.name: UploadPatternChunks
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 3930..4078 Set VRAM write address zero and stream 64-byte unrolled chunks from the source pointer at C600. C634 is the chunk count; zero would wrap to 256 chunks, so valid callers must provide a positive count.

units.name: UploadSpritesAndRunFrame
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4078..4553 Upload 64 Y entries from C100 to VRAM 3F00, then 128 X/pattern bytes from C140 to VRAM 3F80. Saturate the pause debounce counter at 15. A paused frame skips the update chain; otherwise update helpers run according to upload and frame flags. The individual object/audio helper semantics remain for their own source review.

units.name: FinishFrameUpdates
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4553..4559 Run the remaining frame helpers, select bank 6 and call CPU 8000. Clear the pending upload byte when its high bit is set, increment the frame-completion byte and restore the saved 8000-window ROM bank.

units.name: RestoreInterruptRegisters
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4588..4605 Restore alternate and main registers, both index registers and original AF; enable interrupts and return. The original uses RET rather than RETI.

units.name: WriteScrollControlFragment
units.summary: Begin the horizontal-scroll register write with the work byte at C63A.

units.name: WriteVerticalControlFragment
units.summary: Begin the scroll register write with the coordinate byte at C70F.

units.name: SetVramWriteAndCopy
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4636..4662 The first entry sets the VRAM write address from HL. CPU 1025 then copies BC bytes from DE, preserving DE and BC. A zero count wraps, so callers supply a positive size.

units.name: FillVramByteOrWord
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4662..4698 CPU 1036 repeats the byte at DE for BC bytes. CPU 1046 repeats the two-byte word at DE for BC words; it uses stack exchanges as port timing delays.

units.name: CopyVramRectangle
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 4698..4727 HL is destination, DE packed source, B rows and C words per row. Emit both bytes of each word, then advance destination by 64 bytes to the next name-table row. The inner count is widened to BC with B zero; saved BC restores the row count.

units.name: CopyPaletteBytes
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4727..4744 Set the CRAM command from HL and copy B bytes from DE to the VDP data port. Stack exchanges provide the original port timing delay.

units.name: UnpackFourPlaneRle
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4779..4835 Unpack four planes from HL to interleaved VRAM at DE, advancing the base by one after each plane. Tag zero ends a plane; low seven tag bits are the run count. Bit 7 selects literal bytes; otherwise repeat one source byte. Advance VRAM by four per output byte and leave HL at the next plane or stream. The plane helper is CPU 10B8.

units.name: ReadAndReverseVram
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 4936..4991 CPU 1148 copies BC VRAM bytes at DE into RAM HL. CPU 115B reads to D800, then reverses each byte bit by bit and writes it to VRAM HL. This supports mirrored sprite-pattern resources; the transformation itself is exact even where game purpose varies.

units.name: QueuePaletteAndWait
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 5031..5081 Clear the first sixteen palette work bytes, copy sixteen defaults, then overlay a counted palette record from HL. Set C048 bit 7 and wait for its frame consumer to clear the request. The count must fit the 32-byte palette buffer.

units.name: ClearPaletteAndServiceRequests
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 5097..5151 CPU 11E9 clears the 32-byte palette buffer, queues it and waits. CPU 1205 tests the palette request then decrements the control byte until zero before uploading 32 CRAM bytes. The following C641 path is only partially classified.

units.name: FadePaletteTowardBlack
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 5170..5181 Remember the bank and DE palette pointer, then walk attenuation levels 4 down through 0. Wait eight synchronized frames per level and apply the component clamp helper.

units.name: FadePaletteFromBlack
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 5202..5241 Reload the saved palette source and walk attenuation levels 0 through 3, waiting eight synchronized frames each. Select the saved source bank, copy 32 bytes to the palette buffer and restore ROM bank 2 before conversion.

units.name: ClampPaletteComponents
units.summary: Apply a saturating attenuation to all 32 packed SMS palette bytes.

units.name: UpdateObjectBatch
units.summary: C611 selects an object slot through a CPU-word table; C619 rotates the starting slot between frames. IX points to the selected record. A zero type skips the slot; otherwise dispatch through the type table at CPU 5451, then update animation and invoke the bank-2 object helper. Eligible visible objects pass collision helpers once before setting field 25 bit 0. After 18 slots, terminate the sprite-Y list if fewer than64 entries were emitted and queue its frame upload. Pause skips dispatch. Type identities and slot scheduler policy remain unresolved.

units.name: AdvanceObjectAnimation
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 5525..5543 Use the animation ID to select a word from the C09E table. A nonzero descriptor provides frame duration and frame count, followed by frame IDs. Field13 is the countdown and field 14 the frame index; advance and wrap it only while unpaused. Field25 bit 7 suppresses presentation updates in the following continuation.

units.name: SelectObjectFrameResource
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 5579..5616 Read the selected frame ID and resolve it through the C0A0 word table. Copy its chunk count to C61A, presentation byte to object field 21 and payload pointer to C61B. IDs below 79 may replace the queued pattern resource; C602 avoids repeated loads. A four-byte descriptor at CPU 1445 provides bank, conversion flag and source word. The conversion flag selects the mirrored scratch path.

units.name: QueuePatternUpload
units.summary: For mirrored patterns, reverse each source byte into D200 scratch. Queue the resulting source at C600, copy its 64-byte chunk count to C634 and set C614 bit 6. The ISR later uploads these chunks to VRAM zero.

units.name: BuildScrollColumnCoordinates
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6017..6022 C700 flags select forward/reverse coordinate handling. Align the horizontal coordinate to eight-pixel cells and derive parallel VRAM/RAM destination pointers. Extract the half-cell phase into C732 and divide the selected map coordinate by16. Flag bit 0 can bypass this setup into the full-row builder.

units.name: LocateScrollColumnMap
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 6132..6160 Convert the other axis according to direction bit 4, extracting phase C733. Divide its coordinate by16, multiply by the map stride C71F and add the first axis and map-base C723. C72C holds the resulting map cursor; C72E points to a thirteen-entry column scratch buffer at C739.

units.name: BuildScrollColumnTiles
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6214..6220 For each of13 map cells, select map bank C722, read its metatile ID and index an eight-byte record at C726 in bank C725. Select two word pairs using phase C732 and store them in column scratch. Map cursor advances by stride. C733 chooses the output pair offset. Stage flag C652 bit 1 inserts the fixed word 3148 presentation override (bytes 48,31); mark the scroll buffer dirty.

units.name: BuildScrollWindowCoordinates
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6319..6327 Build a complete scroll window rather than one column. Direction flags select signed coordinate conversion, preserve row phase C732 and column phase C733, and compare against prior coordinates through C70A/C70B later in this routine.

units.name: InitializeScrollWindowRows
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6436..6495 Resolve map cell coordinates and base as for the column path. Select RAM buffer C900 or C8C0 from the column phase, compute a64-byte wrap split and initialize thirteen output row iterations. Each iteration builds17 metatiles into the pair of temporary rows C769 and C7AD.

units.name: ExpandScrollWindowMetatiles
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6548..6566 For17 cells, read each map ID in bank C722 and copy its eight-byte record from bank C725 into two four-byte row buffers. Copy the selected phase of the first row into the destination up to its64-byte wrap boundary.

units.name: CopyWrappedScrollRows
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 6631..6642 If the row crosses the64-byte buffer boundary, copy the remainder to its wrapped base. Advance one row and repeat the phase-selected split copy for the second expanded row. A zero remainder bypasses the second copy.

units.name: FinishScrollWindowBuild
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6699..6749 Advance map cursor by stride and repeat thirteen rows. Compare old/new phase coordinates and set dirty/changed flags, then store the new phase. Stage flag C652 bit 1 fills128 words at CE00 with bytes 48,31.

units.name: SelectScrollRebuildPath
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 6780..6821 Retain the relevant scroll flags. Skip rebuilding when direction/state flags prohibit it or the coordinate high byte is zero. Otherwise adjust the RAM destination by64 bytes when the fine coordinate is nonzero and re-enter the scroll-coordinate builder.

units.name: ApplyHorizontalScrollDelta
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6821..6849 Clear the horizontal pending flag and actual-delta word C7F1. The signed8.8 delta at C70C updates a24-bit coordinate split across C712/C714. Negative motion clamps at zero, records actual displacement and updates the circular C710 coordinate modulo0800. Boundary crossings set direction/dirty flags; unrelated pending bits survive.

units.name: ClampHorizontalScrollAndDispatch
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 6952..6978 Positive horizontal motion clamps to the C720 limit; record the actual delta, update the circular coordinate and direction flags, then clear C70C. A boundary crossing invokes a tile rebuild. The following entry performs the parallel second-axis update from C715, unless scroll-state bit 6 routes to the special handler.

units.name: ApplyVerticalScrollDelta
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 7095..7365 Apply the signed8.8 C715 delta to the24-bit coordinate C71B/C71D. Clamp against C728/C72A according to direction and stop repeated boundary transitions with C701 bits 0/1. Apply actual displacement to the display coordinate C717, wrapping its high byte moduloE0, and to the circular tile coordinate C719 modulo0800. Direction changes set C700 bit 4/bit 0 and rebuild pending state. Clear C715 after consuming it; retain unresolved game-specific camera policy.

units.name: CommitScrollToVdp
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 7380..7405 The preceding dirty path jumps back into tile rebuilding. This entry writes C70F to VDP register 8 (horizontal scroll), then consumes scroll-buffer bit 7. Bit0 chooses a full-window upload; otherwise use the narrow column path.

units.name: UploadScrollColumn
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 7405..7424 Write24 tile words to VRAM at 64-byte row intervals, mirroring each word into the RAM tile buffer. Alternate register sets retain the separate VRAM destination/source and RAM mirror pointers.

units.name: UploadScrollWindow
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 7456..7484 Copy02C0 pairs of bytes from C900 to VRAM 3880. This uploads the prepared tile window; a NOP preserves the original VDP write cadence.

units.name: UpdatePlayerInputState
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 7484..7552 IX is the primary object. Push the common movement continuation, then dispatch special state flags or action/direction buttons in priority order. With no input, clear action kind and animation timers and select an idle animation through the facing-aware animation helper. Movement and attacks use their own fragments below.

units.name: SetPlayerCrouchState
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 7562..7587 Set action kind2, choose animation 02 or12 from facing bit 5, and clear animation timers.

units.name: BeginPlayerMoveRight
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 7587..7605 Clear action kind and set horizontal speed 0100. Facing bit 5 selects a direction continuation; the classified opposite-facing fragment clears motion bit 0.

units.name: CommitPlayerMoveRight
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 7628..7644 Motion flag bit 3 prevents this transition. Otherwise select animation from the CPU 1C15 record and tail-call the movement/camera helper.

units.name: BeginPlayerMoveLeft
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 7644..7666 Clear action kind and set horizontal speedFF00. Facing selects a continuation; the classified opposite-facing path sets motion bit 0. Motion bit 2 can reject the transition before animation selection. The adjacent state entries retain the intervening transition.

units.name: SetPlayerActionKindOne
units.summary: Read the previous action kind and set it to 1 before the directional action selection.

units.name: BeginPlayerJumpOrAttack
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 7869..7922 Recognize a newly pressed button5 using the previous controller state. Reset horizontal speed and animation timers, set acceleration 30 and action kind3. Previous action kind chooses specialized continuations. Otherwise load the stage-specific initial vertical speed, select animation 06/16 by facing, enter object type 4 and queue request 90. Probably begins a jump/airborne attack; exact type semantics remain tentative.

units.name: PlayerActionHelper2818
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 7946..7949 Invoke CPU 2818 in this action continuation. Its wider contract needs the consumer review.

units.name: PlayerActionHelper2830
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 7995..7998 Invoke CPU 2830 in this action continuation; the adjacent entries retain the surrounding transition.

units.name: ConsumePlayerActionRequest
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 8035..8048 Require both C07C bits 5/6, otherwise return to ordinary input dispatch. Clear bit 5 when the coordinated request has been accepted.

units.name: BeginPlayerAlternateAttack
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 8065..8112 Require a new button4 press. C632 chooses object type 2 or3 and resets its substate. The following entry sets action kind4, retains selected facing/motion flags, sets horizontal speed to0100 orFF00 and vertical speed 0, then enters type 5 with acceleration 40. These are separate attack-state transitions.

units.name: SetPlayerTypeTen
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 8140..8144 Set the primary object type to0A; surrounding transition logic is unknown.

units.name: InitializePlayerActionAnimation
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 8290..8328 Push common movement continuation. A high state flag redirects to special handling; otherwise initialize substate once, remember the previous action kind at C1DF and select one of two animations. Clear animation timer/index after loading it.

units.name: FinishPlayerActionOnInput
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 8362..8369 Compare current and previous action-button bits and directional bit 1. Field31 selects an alternate release test. When the action/animation can finish, clear timer/substate, return to object type 1 and mask the action button from sampled input. The next state entry runs its collision helper and returns to type 1 when airborne motion flag 7 is absent.

units.name: PollPlayerAttackWhileMoving
units.summary: Return on the collision helper carry result. Release of button5 clears the shared action request. A new button4 press may initialize this movement substate; the attack transition continues through the adjacent player-action entries.

units.name: SelectPlayerDirectionalAttack
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 8495..8499 No horizontal direction returns immediately. Direction bit 3 selects positive versus negative horizontal speed and an associated animation/state parameter pair.

units.name: UpdatePlayerDirectionalAttack
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 8536..8564 An empty animation frame redirects to completion. Otherwise require horizontal direction and select positive/negative speed plus direction-state byte. This fragment stores the low speed byte before the unknown continuation.

units.name: ClearPlayerSubstate
units.summary: Clear the primary substate before the following motion transition.

units.name: UpdatePlayerAirAction
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 8602..8618 Run movement/camera and vertical-motion helpers, then return to type 1 when motion flag 7 clears. Continue only if collision checks permit and button4 is a new press; the classified tail invokes the action-reset helper.

units.name: CheckPlayerLowerScreenBoundary
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 9705..9719 If the extended Y byte is zero, test visible Y against E8/F8. The narrow interval sets type 0B; other paths jump to CPU 2406. The classified return clears carry with XOR A. This appears to distinguish a bottom-edge transition.

units.name: FinalizePrimaryObject
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 10339..10360 C65C low flags choose special continuations. Clear render flag 7, and when state flag 6 is set decrement object timer 15. Separate short continuations clear the render flag again; their surrounding logic is unknown.

units.name: CheckStageTargetPosition
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 10384..10419 Compare scroll/world coordinates C713/C71C and primary object X/Y bytes against the stage target C64C-C651. Mismatch enters ordinary movement; a full match sets primary type 9. Whether this represents an exit or encounter trigger depends on the stage record and remains unresolved.

units.name: MovePlayerHorizontalAndCamera
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 10437..10464 Correct the requested horizontal speed using a collision helper, add it to primary screen X and compare direction-specific screen thresholds10/60/F0. Camera boundary flags determine whether to move the object or write the delta to C70C while holding the primary object at screen X60. Stage flag bit 4 selects an alternate clamp path. The adjacent clamp entries retain the threshold continuations.

units.name: MovePlayerVerticalAndLand
units.summary: Add vertical8.8 speed to primary Y and propagate its carry/borrow to the extended byte. Add acceleration 19 to the speed and update motion flag 6. Probe two tile positions at vertical offsets-4/+3; tile high bits and motion orientation choose collision acceptance. On accepted contact clear the Y fraction, align screen Y to8 pixels and clear airborne flag 7.

units.name: ApplyPrimaryTileFlags
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 10714..10721 Inspect saved tile samples C635/C636. Their high bits determine the contact state; bit 7 selects motion flag 1. Two entries either set or clear airborne flag 7 while retaining facing/direction bits 21.

units.name: ProbePrimaryTileCollisions
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 10824..10831 Probe offsets-4/+3 into C635/C636, then compare tile solidity/orientation against motion flag 1 and set airborne flag 7 when neither permits contact. A following side probe uses facing/direction to sample at offset+7/-8, set side-contact bits 2/3 and return a fine8-pixel correction delta. Tile attributes are only established mechanically as high-bit collision flags.

units.name: SelectPrimaryAnimationByVariant
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 10985..10999 Use the variant byte C0A7 to select a pair of animation bytes; facing bit 5 chooses the second byte. Store the result as the primary animation ID.

units.name: FindAndPositionProjectileSlot
units.summary: A nonzero gameplay countdown blocks spawning. Search C0A8 records starting C280 at 48-byte stride for a free type byte. IY receives the free slot; select a spawn-offset record by primary action kind, facing and variant. Add signed offsets to primary X/Y with carry/borrow, then temporarily use IX for a tile probe.

units.name: InitializeProjectileFromVariant
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 11148..11164 Reject blocked spawn tiles using tile orientation and primary motion flags. A variant-indexed eight-byte record supplies request, type, animation and facing-dependent horizontal speed. Reset animation state, set render flag 0, remember the variant in field 32 and impose a12-tick cooldown. Queue request 91. The slot behaves as a projectile; exact weapon names remain unresolved.

units.name: MoveObjectHorizontalRelativeToCamera
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 14761..14806 Subtract actual camera displacement C7F1 from object horizontal velocity, then update its8.8 screen X and extended byte. Accumulate world position in fields22-24 with signed carry. Stage flag bit 2 restricts a special camera-phase correction to object category 19; a phase change nudges Y by8.

units.name: ProbeObjectLeadingTiles
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 14904..14918 Clear side-contact bit 2 and probe ahead in the direction selected by motion bit 0. Near the screen axis skip the probe. Otherwise tile high flags and orientation choose whether the adjacent map row also blocks; set bit 2 on accepted contact. Clear A on the open return path.

units.name: MoveObjectVerticalAndProbeGround
units.summary: Update object 8.8 Y by vertical speed and add acceleration 19. Motion bit 6 records a speed transition. A following entry probes vertical offsets-4/+3 against tile high flags; accepted contact clears the Y fraction. The remainder of the snap/flag tail appears in the adjacent motion continuation.

units.name: CullObjectByScreenAndWorldRange
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 15114..15134 Screen Y, extended position and motion flags choose visibility/culling paths. World distance from scroll coordinateC713 uses40/80 thresholds to retain, defer or remove an object. The classified terminal branch sets object type 62; the exact game role of deferred type 62 remains uncertain.

units.name: ClearObjectAndPostprocess
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 15291..15332 Clear type/substate/animation/velocities and selected render/state bytes, then return through a common postprocessor with carry set. Ordinary completion clears carry. Global C65C bit 0 enables an extra state-flag 2 path that starts an eight-tick animation timer when carry is clear.

units.name: ReadTileAtObjectOffset
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 15758..15777 IX points to an object; B/C are signed screen-axis probe offsets. Adjust X by the hardware scroll byte, align both axes to8 pixels and index the RAM tile-attribute buffer based at C881. Return its attribute byte in A.

units.name: UpdateChasingObject
units.summary: Run range culling and camera-relative movement, then dispatch substates1/2/3. Out-of-plane extended X values choose recovery paths. Ground/contact helpers can enter substate 3 and stop vertical speed. The object identity is unresolved.

units.name: ChooseChaserDirection
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 15886..15921 Compare primary X with this object and combine facing/direction bits to choose animation 71/73 and signed horizontal speed. Several single-instruction fragments expose alternate substate/animation choices; the intervening setup is retained in the adjacent entries.

units.name: CheckChaserAxisDistance
units.summary: Take absolute screen X, compare against10 and invoke the tile probe only outside that near-axis interval before the chase continuation.

units.name: StopChaserHorizontalSpeedLow
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 16134..16138 Clear the low X-velocity byte before the adjacent high-byte and timed-wait continuation.

units.name: TickChaserTimer
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 16150..16153 Decrement object field 40; its initialization and exact timing role remain unresolved.

units.name: MoveChaserAlongGround
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 16192..16243 Near the screen axis choose zero horizontal speed; otherwise probe ahead and choose0180 orFE80 when unobstructed. Store velocity, run vertical movement and ground collision, then stop the low horizontal-speed byte when airborne flag 7 clears, with the adjacent contact and timed-state entries supplying the continuation.

units.name: InitializeObjectTypeThirtyNine
units.summary: Use initial animation 70 and motion flags 21. Set category 9, acceleration 40, type 39, clear render flag 0 and return. The adjacent alternate entry supplies its own initial parameters.

units.name: RemoveObjectOnTileImpact
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 18886..18915 Move relative to the camera, then require extended X zero and visible X>=8. Probe the current tile and compare its orientation with motion flag 1. On accepted contact queue requestA8 and tail-call the object-clear helper.

units.name: MoveObjectWithoutAcceleration
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 19935..19972 Subtract actual camera displacement from horizontal velocity and update screen X with extended carry/borrow. Separately add vertical velocity to screen Y and propagate carry/borrow. This entry does not apply acceleration.

units.name: UpdateTimedHudState
units.summary: C653 bit 7 enables this state. Clear C079 bit 7, initialize once using bit 6 and decrement the following timer in its later continuation. Initialization and presentation are handled by the adjacent continuation.

units.name: UpdateGlobalObjectTimer
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 21334..21340 C65C bit 7 enables the global object condition. Low-nibble state chooses alternate handlers; otherwise decrement the16-bit C65D timer and branch at zero. A separate classified exit clears the state byte. Gameplay meaning remains unresolved.

units.name: UploadPackedDecimalHud
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 21830..21838 Consume dirty flag C078 bit 7. Convert the six nibbles at C040-C042 into tile numbers at VRAM 3814, suppressing leading zeroes until a nonzero digit. Each tile gets attribute09; append the terminating tile pair.

units.name: UploadHudTileRun
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 21889..21897 Consume dirty flag C06B bit 7 and write C06E tile IDs from C06F to VRAM 384A, each with attribute09. This appears to be a variable-length HUD field.

units.name: UploadHudFourCellMeter
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 21923..21931 Consume C079 dirty flag. Clamp C07A to4, emit that many tile2C entries at VRAM 3838, then fill the remaining cells with tile0, all with attribute09.

units.name: UploadHudTwoRows
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 21983..21995 C07C bit 7 requests this update; bit 6 diverts to a timed continuation. Otherwise clear the dirty flag and upload two rows of eight tile IDs from C082 with attribute09 at VRAM 3824/3864. The alternate tail decrements C64A.

units.name: ScanStageObjectEvents
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 22395..22400 Select ROM bank 4. Unless both scroll flags 0C are set, select a region pointer through C659/C71E and index six-byte event records by C63E. Compare each event coordinate with camera position and direction, advance or retreat the event index, and retain the payload cursor at C63C. A zero event type terminates processing; high event-index bits select stage-progress versus ordinary object state tracking.

units.name: ClaimStageProgressEvent
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 22532..22555 Low six event-index bits select StageProgressSlots. Bits6/7 choose one of two claim policies: reject completed/already claimed slots, then set progress bit 4 or5. These flags prevent duplicate stage-event activation.

units.name: SpawnStageEventObject
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 22618..22651 Ordinary event IDs select D000 state bytes; reject claimed/completed entries, set bit 7 and search five48-byte object slots after C2E0. Undo the claim if no slot is free. Store the event ID in field 32 and initialize type, Y and direction-adjusted X from its record; clear fractions and extended bytes. Specialized event handlers share this service. The shared initialization body also accepts an existing object through the HL-to-IY adapter; that entry neither allocates nor writes field32.

units.name: InitializeAndScanStageEventWindow
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 22727..22732 Select bank 4 and stage pointer tableA570. Capture the camera coordinate as a256-pixel event window C655-C657. Index six-byte records by C63E and adjust the initial scan to direction. Compare event coordinates against the window while advancing over records. Push a continuation so each accepted event returns to the scan; zero type skips its spawn.

units.name: LocateStageEventOnScreen
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 22926..23013 Resolve event Y relative to C71C and the C728 bound, retaining only positions24..184. Save this at C65B. High event-ID flags route to stage progress claim policies, which set bit 4/5 after checking completion flags.

units.name: SpawnWindowEventObject
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 23076..23094 Claim the D000 event byte, find one of five free48-byte slots and roll back the claim if full. Initialize type, camera-relative X and computed Y, clear fractional/extended position and advance event index. Field32 links the spawned object to its persistent event state. The shared initialization body also accepts an existing object through the HL-to-IY adapter; that entry neither allocates nor writes field32.

units.name: ConsumePresentationRequest
units.summary: C61E bit 7 enables this path; clear it once consumed before the presentation transfer.

units.name: UpdatePaletteTransitionState
units.summary: Bonus exit graphics transfer: zero idle, phase two palette defaults, phase three done; otherwise initialize once and copy bank-9 graphics in 0100-byte chunks. Legacy palette label retained as an alias.

units.name: RestorePaletteTransitionDefaults
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 25255..25266 Restore the final 15 palette bytes from CPU 58A9 to C05A, then request upload and finish bonus exit phase three in the continuation below.

units.name: DispatchAcrobaticObject
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 27057..27113 Update the object helper, index a substate word table and jump through HL. Initialization sets category 1A, animation 60, screen position(A8,E0), negative horizontal velocity and substate 1, then loads bank 8 RLE graphics to VRAM 06C0. The object identity is unresolved; its later behavior is a jumping pursuit.

units.name: AdvanceAcrobaticObject
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 27116..27221 Clear transient state flag 7. Approach until X<C0, then enter substate 2. Another entry launches with vertical speedFB80 and acceleration 30, chooses horizontal direction toward the primary object and animation 68/62. After vertical movement, velocity-transition flag 6 advances animation/substate 4; state flag 4 selects substate 7 instead.

units.name: WaitAcrobaticLanding
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 27257..27275 Move vertically, clear transient state flag 7 and route state flag 4 to its special continuation. When airborne flag 7 clears, enter substate 5.

units.name: ClampAcrobaticScreenX
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 27484..27494 Apply camera-relative movement, then clamp visible X into 08..F8. The two short clamp continuations preserve the original unknown gaps.

units.name: InitializeMovingGroupController
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 28939..29002 Dispatch by substate after the object helper. Initialize category 1B, animation 59 and position(50,18), then seed six48-byte child slots atC340 with type 8E. Until camera boundary flag 3 sets, request horizontal scroll20 and matching object speed; the boundary path clears its speed low byte.

units.name: AllocateGridObjectPosition
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 29011..29040 Dispatch through a substate table. Initialization scans16 occupancy bytes at C800 for a clear bit 0; the full-table path calls CPU 733E. Claim a cell, remember its index in field 43, derive Y from its low two bits at 48-pixel spacing and X from the upper two bits at 32-pixel spacing plusC0. Set category 1A and substate 1. Later state/helper flags choose substate 3 or consume state flag 7. The grid entity game identity is unresolved.

units.name: PositionObjectRelativeToScroll
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 29535..29558 Take a coordinate from CPU 6F9B, subtract the negated hardware scroll byte and store extended screen X, then tail-call the common object helper.

units.name: TestObjectTimerForty
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 29627..29632 Return field 40 in A with Z set if zero. Callers determine its timer semantics.

units.name: LookupCpuWordByIndex
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30028..30038 A is an unchecked word index and HL the table base. Return the selected little-endian CPU pointer in HL; preserve no bounds information.

units.name: DispatchTimedFacingObject
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30434..30481 Move with camera, dispatch through a substate word table, and initialize category 1A, position(A0,C0), field 41=8 and field 43=20. The active state calls three object-specific helpers; their exact sequence meaning is unresolved.

units.name: ConsumeObjectStatePair
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30678..30690 Clear state flags after sampling. Only simultaneous bitsA0 invoke the animation/state helper with value 5D; other combinations return.

units.name: ChooseTimedFacingAnimation
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30728..30756 Every32 ticks compare object extended X and primary X+40 (saturated atFF). Choose the left/right helper using that threshold. A following entry waits for exact threshold equality before requesting animation 5A.

units.name: ResetTimedFacingAnimation
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30797..30818 Invoke the facing helper, enter substate 1, set animation 5B and clear animation timer/index. The later classified fragment sets motion flags 20.

units.name: SetNegativeHorizontalSpeedAndLookup
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30844..30867 Set motion flags 21 and horizontal speedFF80. The separate CPU 7689 entry indexes a little-endian word table in HL using A and returns that word.

units.name: AnimateBackgroundStrip
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30867..30877 C6B0 bit 7 enables a periodic three-frame strip. A signed timer reloads2, cycles an index modulo3 and copies a58-byte frame into C6BA unless bit 6 suppresses animation changes. Camera coordinate/8 indexes CPU 7811; derive the visible clipped span and start offset using a29-cell width.

units.name: UploadClippedBackgroundStrip
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 30969..31022 Skip empty spans. Derive a name-table destination from C6B5 and the clipped start, then upload twice the visible-cell count from C6BA. A following C6B0 bit 0 path decrements C6B9; its continuation is unknown.

units.name: InitializeLargeEncounterController
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 31329..31407 Initialize extended X, category 19, background-strip state and object type 6D. Fields40/41 form a0384 timer; field 45 is8 and presentation60. The active path clears horizontal speed and decrements the16-bit timer before choosing its timed continuation. This probably controls a large scrolling encounter.

units.name: ChooseEncounterHorizontalState
units.summary: Dispatch substates0..3, compare extended/screen X against B0/D0/70 and compare distance from primary X with16 pixels. Choose approach/retreat helpers or substate 3; the state transitions continue in the adjacent entries.

units.name: MoveEncounterAndCameraOppositely
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 31539..31555 Request camera delta0080 and object speedFF80; the opposite entry requests FF80 camera delta and 0080 object speed, including the adjacent high-byte store.

units.name: AdvanceEncounterVerticalTargets
units.summary: Field43 indexes CPU 7B25 target Y values. At the target, field 42 selects ascending or descending indices, toggling its direction at 0 and 2. The adjacent motion entries retain the intermediate state updates.

units.name: MoveEncounterVerticallyAndSignal
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 31700..31719 Set vertical camera delta0100 orFF00 using field 42 direction. A later fragment decrements field 44; another queues requestA5 and clears transient state flag 7. The event timing between these fragments is unresolved.

units.name: PositionEncounterBackgroundStrip
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 31806..31850 For nonnegative extended Y, subtract00B0 and divide by8. Results below 20 become the strip destination C6B5 and enable animation by clearing C6B0 bit 6; out-of-range coordinates disable animation through that bit.

units.name: InitializeAndBlinkStageMarker
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 32232..32239 Initialize once using substate bit 0. StageIndex selects a four-byte record at CPU 7C55, or C017 chooses record 19. Store animation and screen X/Y and clear fractions/extended coordinates and counter 26. A new button5 press clears C017 and removes the marker; otherwise alternate render flag 7 on even counter ticks when C017 is zero. Probably a stage/briefing marker.

units.name: AppendObjectSprites
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 44800..44874 Render flag 7 suppresses output. Category12 and facing select a pattern base through C0A4; C61A supplies sprite count. Reject totals above 64, reserve Y and X/pattern buffer space, then add signed per-sprite offsets to object position with extended-byte clipping. Sprite records are three bytes: Y offset, X offset and pattern offset.

units.name: ClipAndEmitObjectSprites
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 44890..44900 Clip extended Y/X and avoid Y=D0, which terminates the hardware sprite list, by substitutingD1. Out-of-range X hides the matching Y entry withD1. Emit X and pattern-base+offset into C140 and advance the three-byte source. Repeat for every reserved sprite; a rejected sprite still occupies its slot.

units.name: ScheduleObjectCollisionPass
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 44975..45083 Skip when camera flag 3 is set. Cycle a four-way collision phase in C649. The primary-player phase ignores transient state7 and action kind3, then selects an action/variant/facing hitbox and tests seven object pointers. Certain target categories set C632 to1; stage flag 3 restricts that special result.

units.name: CheckPrimaryAgainstObjectGroup
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 45102..45149 Require an active primary presentation and no transient state7. Build its hitbox and test fourteen object pointers, clearing target state bit 4 before each test and setting it on accepted collision. Remaining response bytes are unknown.

units.name: CheckProjectileObjectCollisions
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 45214..45301 Test the C280/C2B0/C2E0 projectile-like slots against seven object pointers. On collision set transient state7, select the replacement type through variant tableAF49 and reset substate. Type16 filters target categories; another helper may modify target state flags using projectile direction. The shared response queues requestA5; exact damage rules remain unresolved.

units.name: CheckPrimaryActionFiveCollision
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 45390..45405 Only primary action kind5 with a nonzero presentation reaches this hitbox setup. State flag 7 suppresses it; the following group-test bytes are unknown.

units.name: BuildCurrentCollisionBounds
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 45569..45603 A indexes five-byte hitbox records at DE. Skip the leading control byte, add Y offset/height and X offset/width to the object position, and cache bounds at C60D-C610. Saturate the right edge toFF on overflow.

units.name: TestCollisionBoundsAgainstObject
units.summary: HL supplies an object pointer; IY becomes the candidate. Reject different plane bit 1, nonzero extended position, empty type, transient state7 or absent presentation. Resolve its five-byte hitbox, saturating horizontal offsets/edges at 00/FF, and test interval overlap against C60D-C610. Return0 for no overlap and 1/2 for accepted cases; their gameplay distinction depends on the caller. Motion flag 4 records a plane mismatch.

units.name: AdjustHudMeterValue
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 46356..46372 Treat A as a signed adjustment to the C06C meter and compare it with the C06D limit. Positive overflow can raise that limit; negative handling and intermediate clamp bytes are partly unknown. Retain this mechanical name until health/energy semantics are established.

units.name: BuildHudMeterTiles
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 46397..46433 Use ceil(C06D/2) cells initially filled with tile32. C06C contributes full tile30 per two units and tile31 for an odd remainder. Set C06B bit 7 to queue the tile run for the frame HUD uploader.

units.name: UpdateSoundDriver
units.summary: Data; Static; physical 98608..98816 Exact byte-transition boundaries and current code conflicts were checked in the phase-one review. This supports generic non-code storage only; padding, decoded graphics and original generator remain unproven. Uniform $FF non-code byte run; specific use/fill purpose unresolved. Code; Observed; physical 98816..98885 ROM bank 6 CPU 8000 is the per-frame sound entry. Save the driver mode in alternate AF, retain the shared channel result pointer in alternate HL and service priorities, tempo, fades, command requests and channel arbitration. Nonzero driver mode processes ten32-byte channel records from DE0E, with a special rhythm-channel entry at loop index 4. Zero selects seven records starting DE6E and the separately labeled slot-specific channel readers. This is the audio record layout, distinct from the48-byte gameplay objects.

units.name: ArbitrateSharedSoundChannels
units.summary: DF2E bit 7 enables a shared channel. DF0E activity and the shared flags/type determine whether DE6E/DEAE channel suppression bit 2 is set. This prevents competing voices from writing the same hardware channel.

units.name: TickSoundTempo
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 98969..98977 If DE01 is nonzero, decrement and reload it from DE02 on expiration. Then increment duration counters in seven 32-byte channel records. A zero tempo divider leaves the counters unchanged.

units.name: SelectQueuedSoundRequest
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 98994..99013 Inspect three pending request bytes DE04-DE06. Bit7 marks a request; index priority table 8267 with request-1. A high-bit priority routes immediately; ordinary priority replaces DE03 only if it meets the current DE07 priority. Consume the accepted queue byte by clearing it.

units.name: FadeSoundChannels
units.summary: DE0A is the remaining fade-step count and DE0B its18-frame divider. Each step increments six channel attenuation bytes toward16. At completion stop sound. In FM mode begin programming instrument/volume registers through ports F0/F1, continuing through the adjacent upload loop.

units.name: ClearFmRegister
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 99380..99389 Write A as the FM register address atF0, wait the original timing helper and write zero toF1. This fragment is entered from other audio setup.

units.name: InitializeFmRegisters
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 99389..99413 Send18 register/value pairs from CPU 8255 through FM portsF0/F1, retaining BC and inserting the original bus-delay helper between writes.

units.name: DispatchSoundRequest
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 99713..99724 Only requests with bit 7 set are pending. Values81..8F start music-like sequences;90..B2 select effects, B3 selects a special sequence andB4..B8 index a command-handler word table. Values>=B9 stop sound. These ranges describe dispatch mechanics; individual request names remain unresolved.

units.name: StartMusicSequence
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 99787..99836 Convert requests81+ into sequence indices, stop prior sound and initialize FM setup. Load tempo from829E and choose the sequence table/channel base according to driver mode. Resolve a word through 84E3, then initialize the sequence channels. The index is unchecked in this fragment.

units.name: StartEffectSequence
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 99836..99851 Convert90+ requests to effect table indices and choose FM/PSG descriptors. Descriptor channel types10/14/C0/E0/A0 choose channel storage and voice suppression. Several paths stop shared voices or emit PSG mute valuesDF/FF before initializing channels. Priority and ownership depend on the recorded channel flags.

units.name: InitializeSoundChannelRecords
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 99997..100055 A descriptor count controls channel initialization: copy nine parameter bytes, set stack offset 20, duration1 and clear subsequent work bytes. Advance destination by32 bytes and call the FM/PSG output initializer through a stacked continuation. After all channels consume the request by writing80 to SoundRequest. Zero channel count would wrap.

units.name: LookupSoundDescriptorWord
units.summary: A indexes a little-endian pointer table in HL. Return the selected word in BC. This bounded caller contract supplies the descriptor domain.

units.name: TickFmRhythmChannel
units.summary: Increment elapsed ticks and read a new stream token at duration expiry. TokenE0+ dispatches sequence commands, values<7F use the common note path, and the intermediate range updates the rhythm register shadow with expanded percussion flags. Write FM register 0E at note expiry and clear it two ticks before the next event. The final continuation enters the ordinary FM-channel timer path.

units.name: ApplySoundPitchSlide
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 100189..100192 Use signed field 17 to update the low pitch byte with carry/borrow into the high pitch byte. Channel mode flags choose the correction path; changes mark the register dirtythe adjacent borrow path updates the pitch high byte.

units.name: WriteFmChannelState
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 100267..100278 Suppressed channels return. Gate/retrigger fields and channel tick result decide whether to emit pitch, key-on or silence. Resolve note pitch through CPUABD8 when required, apply envelope and optional pitch normalization, then write F-number low/high at channel registers and instrument/volume at channel+20 through F0/F1. Preserve the original timing delays. Muting writes zero to the channel high/key register; individual flag combinations remain described by their consumers rather than game labels.

units.name: ResolveSoundEnvelope
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 100450..100460 Index a word table with A, then apply an envelope byte at field 13. High-bit bytes are control markers:80 resets,83 advances the cursor and other markers set the muted field. Ordinary bytes advance the envelope cursor and add a pitch delta to DE. FM mode detects a changed high pitch/register byte and sets its dirty bit.

units.name: ReadSoundNoteAndDuration
units.summary: Clear channel flag 0 and update an encoded attenuation ramp if present. Read tokens from the channel stream: E0+ invokes commands, lower notes resolve through the pitch table and update pitch bytes. Optional flags read extra slide parameters. Duration bytes scale by field 2 (repeated addition), while negative tokens can reuse field 21 last duration. Reset envelope/tick/gate work fields, save the advanced stream pointer and return80 as the new-note indication.

units.name: ResolveRawSoundPitch
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 100673..100703 Read a two-byte raw pitch and apply signed transpose with carry/borrow. The following normalization helper scales the pitch, chooses a block exponent and subtracts0757 to form the FM register encoding. Zero pitch and small/high values take separate normalization branches.

units.name: LookupNoteAndDispatchSequenceCommand
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 100772..100821 Notes80+ use one of two word pitch tables (8CBD/8D4F) selected by driver mode, after adding transpose. CommandsEC+ index a handler word table; lower commands jump to the shared command decoder. The pushed87D1 continuation resumes note decoding after a command handler returns.

units.name: AddSoundAttenuation
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 100879..100891 Ignore this adjustment during a fade. Otherwise add the stream byte to the channel attenuation and enter the shared attenuation-update handler.

units.name: UploadCustomFmInstrument
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 100891..100924 Select the channel high register, then upload eight custom instrument bytes through F0/F1 with bus-delay calls. Return DE positioned one byte before the next command token, as required by the dispatcher continuation.

units.name: AdjustSoundTranspose
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 100974..100977 Driver mode selects absolute versus accumulated stream handling. Advance DE and add the command parameter to the signed transpose field 5.

units.name: SetSoundAttenuation
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 100997..101004 Ignore changes during a fade. Mask the stream parameter to a four-bit attenuation value; suppressed channels stop here. Driver mode routes to the FM register writer or the PSG writer.

units.name: SetSoundInstrumentOrEnvelope
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101051..101054 Driver mode selects command interpretation. One path stores field 7 unless parameter 80 means unchanged; the other ignores parameter 4 and active fades before updating the same instrument/control field. A separate entry stores the stream byte as envelope selector field 6.

units.name: JumpSoundStream
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101110..101116 Read a little-endian word at DE into DE and decrement it so the common decoder continuation advances to the exact destination.

units.name: StopSoundChannel
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101224..101240 Release shared-channel suppression, clear request priority and deactivate this channel. The PSG branch writes channel+1F to port 7F as a mute. Other mode-specific cleanup follows outside the classified fragment.

units.name: RestoreSharedFmVoice
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101323..101380 An early return discards two stacked decoder continuations. The following voice-release path writes channel hardware state and restores shared FM instrument/volume registers34/35 from saved channel records when competing effects release their suppression bits.

units.name: CallSoundSubsequence
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101410..101437 Read a target word, push the return stream pointer into the channel-local stack indexed by field 9 (decremented by2), then return with DE=target-1. Stack bounds are enforced by valid sequence data, not this fragment.

units.name: ReturnOrLoopSoundSubsequence
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101437..101478 Pop a stream pointer from the channel-local stack and advance its index by2. The next entry selects a loop counter at channel+18+parameter, initializes it from the stream when zero, decrements and branches through the command jump path while nonzero. Expired loops skip the target word.

units.name: StopAllSound
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101480..101597 Preserve main pointers/counts, clear the request/control header and reset ten32-byte channel records and their loop counters. Set control byteDE08 toE4, send eleven PSG initialization/mute bytes and clear FM key registers 20..25. Restore registers before returning; hardware compatibility beyond these observed PSG/FM port writes is not implied.

units.name: SoundPortDelay
units.summary: Code; Observed; physical 101608..101611 A push/pop of HL provides the original short FM port delay and preserves HL.

units.name: WritePsgAttenuation
units.summary: Code; Static; physical 102064..102076 Combine four-bit attenuation with channel latch bits, add10 and send the resulting PSG command to port 7F, then return to the channel service.

units.name: CopierPrefix
units.summary: 512-byte copier envelope; not mapped into CPU ROM.

units.name: MainModeHandlers
units.summary: DispatchMainMode indexes by MainMode low nibble; nine little-endian CPU addresses in fixed ROM. Nine CPU-word main-mode dispatch entries.

units.name: CartridgeHeader
units.summary: Physical header includes the copier prefix in this offset; checksum, product and size fields are preserved verbatim. SMS TMR SEGA cartridge header.

units.name: StageSpriteListPointers
units.summary: LoadStageSpriteResources uses StageIndex 0..18; pointers remain in effective ROM bank 15 at CPU 8000-BFFF. 19 little-endian pointers to bank 15 stage sprite-resource lists.

units.name: StageSpriteList00
units.summary: First byte counts entries. Each has bank byte, VRAM destination word and compressed CPU source word, then a word byte-count. Nonzero count adds VRAM source/destination words for ReverseVramBits. Lists are copied to D520 before bank switching; resource stream banks are effective16-KiB indices. units.name: StageScrollHeaderPointers
units.summary: Nineteen stage pointers followed by nineteen 12-byte source records. The consumer copies 16 bytes from each source, so adjacent copy windows overlap by four bytes; do not turn the source stride into 16. Copied fields include camera/section/bank/base values; the last four destination bytes are replaced during camera-pair initialization.

units.name: ProbeControllerThLines
units.summary: Drive both controller TH outputs high, then low, and compare the corresponding input bits. Return FF only when both readings follow the driven level, otherwise zero. Initialization saves this capability result; the board/region interpretation remains tentative.

units.name: InitializeMachineServices
units.summary: Continue reset with audio quieting, low-RAM clearing and the DF-port setup. A bounded nested addition loop provides settling time before the TH-line and FM probes. Disable interrupts again, reset SP, acknowledge VDP status and stream the 22-byte register setup. Clear gameplay RAM, fill the palette buffer, map bank 2 and expand the font source to VRAM 2000. Select initial mode 80 and enable display interrupts before falling through to the main loop. Calls into window 2 require the effective mapped bank; they do not establish a persistent bank contract.

units.name: ProbeFmRegisterLatch
units.summary: Temporarily set memory-control bit 2, then test seven alternating values through F2. Count matching masked readbacks; only seven successes enable the saved FM-present flag. Write the resulting enable bit to F2 and restore the saved memory-control value. This cartridge-enabled static view does not establish execution aliases with the cartridge disabled.

units.name: ReservedImmediateReturn
units.summary: A direct-flow return stub. It changes no registers or state; the following bytes remain unknown.

units.name: InitializeAttractDisplay
units.summary: Finish clearing the mode byte pair and reset the text/display service. Disable interrupts while clearing sprite/game RAM, expanding bank-2 and bank-9 graphics and copying a 12-byte setup block to the stage work area. Select name-table base 3800, re-enable interrupts and tail-call the text writer with CPU 027B. Those source addresses belong to the explicitly selected banks.

units.name: BeginAttractFadeOnStageFlag
units.summary: Stage-work flag bit 3 advances the mode delay and starts a 16-step fade with the input-sequence flag set to 80. Return without changes while that bit is clear.

units.name: AdvanceAttractPageSequence
units.summary: Continue only when the preceding timer result is zero. Reload six ticks and advance the page index, loading a word from CPU 038A into the display request and arming it with 80. After index 13, wait for the 16-frame condition counter, advance the mode, copy five attract-state bytes, map bank 2 and transfer to its B2E1 continuation.

units.name: ResetTextServiceTail
units.summary: Tail-call the shared text/display reset service; the caller's return remains on the stack.

units.name: AttractReturnStub
units.summary: Immediate return reached from the attract-mode control flow. No state change occurs here.

units.name: DrawAttractScorePanel
units.summary: Upload four fixed tile/name-table spans through the shared VRAM writer, then render two three-byte packed-decimal fields from C040 and C013 at their panel positions. The last decimal-render call is a tail call.

units.name: FinishInterruptGuardedVramWrite
units.summary: Finish the caller-prepared VRAM transfer, enable interrupts and return. Source, destination and count are supplied by the preceding setup.

units.name: FinishLifeLossTransition
units.summary: Mark the current flag byte, arm the transition byte and wait 240 frames through the condition service. Issue sound request 09, clear session bits 0 and 2, then decrement the signed HUD/life counter. A nonnegative result selects mode 5; exhaustion selects mode 7. Both paths join the existing mode-transition setup.

units.name: ArmStageClearWait
units.summary: Set the current flag's high bit, arm the transition state and initialize the 240-frame condition counter. This fragment continues into the shared frame-wait path below.

units.name: RunBonusShootingLoop
units.summary: Initialize the bonus scene, request sound 82 and set the service countdown. Each frame checks the bonus completion bit, services shooting input and wave spawning, updates objects, then explicitly maps bank 2 for its target-collision scan. Loop until completion, seed the bonus cursor state, issue request 02 and enter bonus score conversion. This is the shooting bonus path; it does not establish an ending or credits route.

units.name: AdvanceStageCameraSection
units.summary: Clear the forward-section request and increment the section index. Map bank 9, select the stage camera table through AA72, then index four-byte section entries and copy the selected coordinate word to both camera targets. The trailing reverse entry clears the opposite request and decrements the index before joining the existing shared lookup.

units.name: SelectDeferredMode81
units.summary: Store 81 as the main mode and return; the main mode service handles its deferred transition.

units.name: WaitForFrameWhilePaused
units.summary: Map audio bank 6 and mute it, then wait for FrameCompleted. Consume each frame flag and update objects while pause remains set. Continue waiting until the pause latch clears, then return. The loop depends on frame interrupts rather than a CPU busy-delay duration.

units.name: DivideDoubleWordByWord
units.summary: Run 16 restoring-division steps with DE supplying the shifting dividend/quotient and HL the remainder; BC is the divisor. Carry from the shift or a successful subtraction sets the quotient bit by incrementing E. A failed subtraction restores HL. No zero-divisor guard is supplied here.

units.name: ReadAttractInputSequence
units.summary: Interpret the bank-4 prerecorded controller sequence through IX=C00B. Positive counts repeat one controller byte; counts with bit 7 set select a literal run of low-seven-bit length. IX+1 is the position/count and IX+3/+4 the stream pointer. Advance to the next record when its count is exhausted; a zero record sets the sequence's completion bit. GameplayController and ControllerState receive the repeated form; the literal form updates GameplayController as encoded.

units.name: ResetFromAudioService
units.summary: Call the current window-2 audio reset entry, then jump to fixed CPU 00BA for machine initialization. The caller must provide the matching audio-bank view for the first call.

units.name: CompleteHorizontalScrollRegisterWrite
units.summary: Complete the VDP register-8 write begun above, then select register 10 with the caller's next data byte. Restore AF, enable interrupts and return. The two-write VDP control protocol makes these bytes part of the scroll update, not an independent data table.

units.name: CompleteVerticalScrollRegisterWrite
units.summary: Complete the VDP register-8 selection and join the shared scroll-register exit above. The relative branch preserves the caller's existing AF save.

units.name: WriteStridedVramRunStream
units.summary: The first entry repeats the existing transfer service four times with adjacent source starts. The following stream entry reads a nonzero run byte: low seven bits are the count and high bit chooses advancing source versus repeating one byte. Each output writes one VRAM byte, then advances the destination by four. Zero ends the stream. Paired EX(SP),HL operations provide delay while preserving the saved return; they do not consume inline parameters.

units.name: FinishTextPaletteSelection
units.summary: Repeat the preceding comparison while it remains nonzero, then load the following selector byte and copy one palette entry through the shared palette helper. HL's preceding scan context is supplied by the text service.

units.name: FinishMirroredPatternConversion
units.summary: Advance input/output pointers and decrement the remaining conversion-byte count. Rejoin the byte-reversal loop while BC is nonzero, then restore the saved source pointer. This is the missing continuation of the mirrored-pattern scratch conversion.

units.name: SetPlayerFacingRightAndIdleSequence
units.summary: Clear motion flag bit 5, reset both primary animation timers and select sequence CPU 1C15. Continue through the shared player motion update. Bit 5 is the facing selector used by the adjacent left-facing entry.

units.name: SetPlayerFacingLeftAndIdleSequence
units.summary: Set motion flag bit 5, reset the animation timers and select the same idle transition sequence before the shared player update.

units.name: PlayerMotionUpdateTail
units.summary: Tail-call the common player motion update at CPU 2690 with the current object state intact.

units.name: SelectPlayerActionFromInputBits
units.summary: The previous action must equal one to enter directional action selection. Controller bit 2 selects one existing branch and bit 3 another; with neither set, reset animation timers and select sequence CPU 1C41. Other prior actions join the established action continuation.

units.name: SetPlayerDirectionalWalkVelocity
units.summary: The first entry sets X velocity +0080; the alternate entry sets FF80 (-0080), both in 8.8 units. A facing change adjusts motion bits 0/5 and resets the animation timers. Existing obstacle/action bits can divert to CPU 1C35; otherwise both directions select the same walk sequence and join the common player motion update.

units.name: StartPlayerHighJump
units.summary: Keep the earlier carry-based rejection. Otherwise mark scroll motion, clear Y acceleration and set upward Y velocity FA00 (-6 pixels/frame in 8.8 units). Facing chooses animation 08 or 18, sound AC is requested, and object type 6/substate zero enters the existing jump continuation.

units.name: StartPlayerShortJump
units.summary: Keep the earlier carry rejection; otherwise mark scroll motion, set upward velocity FD38 and choose facing-dependent animation 07/17. Set type 7 and substate zero before the existing jump-motion continuation. The encoded velocity is exact; the short-jump name reflects its smaller upward magnitude.

units.name: StartTimedPlayerAction
units.summary: Enter player object type 8, clear its substate, choose animation 21 and initialize field 40 to 80. The later action service owns that timer and input behavior.

units.name: InitializePlayerKnockbackAndActionChange
units.summary: Initialize knockback with facing/state-dependent horizontal velocity -0100 or +0100, upward velocity FE00, acceleration 30, a 30-tick local timer and sound 93. The following entry pushes the common player continuation and branches around protected/recovery states. For a new action it resets animation timing, selects a sound from the hitbox variant, saves the previous action in C1DF and chooses one of two transition sequences before setting action kind 5.

units.name: PlayerActionReturnStub
units.summary: Immediate return in the player-action flow; no state changes occur in this fragment.

units.name: RestartPlayerActionSequence
units.summary: Service the shared action helper, clear both animation timers and restart sequence CPU 1F90 through the animation sequencer.

units.name: StorePlayerHorizontalVelocityAndFlags
