units.summary: Complete the FM instrument/attenuation register byte from adjacent high/low nibbles, write F1 and use the established delay helper. Repeat for the caller-supplied channel count, then return.

units.name: SelectNoiseEffectRecordAndMuteHardware
units.summary: Select the DF2E effect record, emit FF/DF/E7 to quiet the shared PSG noise/tone state and join the common effect initialization at CPU 849D.

units.name: SelectFirstAudioRecordInitializer
units.summary: Set DE to the DE0E channel record and join the shared initialization path. This is a record address, not a stream pointer.

units.name: SelectFourthAudioRecordInitializer
units.summary: Set DE to the DE6E channel record and join the same shared initializer.

units.name: SuppressPsgNoiseOwnerForEffect
units.summary: Emit PSG noise latch E7 and mark the DECE record suppressed before the following effect setup.

units.name: MutePsgToneTwoAndResetNoiseLatch
units.summary: Emit DF and E7, then continue the caller-selected channel setup.

units.name: SuppressPsgToneTwoOwnerForEffect
units.summary: Emit C0/00 to the PSG tone latch/data pair and set suppression bit 2 in DEAE before continuing initialization.

units.name: PropagateAudioPitchBorrow
units.summary: Decrement the audio pitch high byte and rejoin the shared pitch-update continuation. This is the borrow counterpart to the surrounding low-byte arithmetic.

units.name: JoinAudioPitchUpdate
units.summary: Join the existing audio pitch-update continuation without an additional state change.

units.name: DiscardAudioHelperReturn
units.summary: Discard the immediate helper return and return to the outer caller. The stack-sensitive exit is intentional and contains no inline data.

units.name: AdjustDurationScaleFromPairedOperand
units.summary: Use the alternate flag state to choose one of two adjacent operand bytes, leaving DE at the second byte in either path. Add that byte to the audio duration-scale field and return.

units.name: AdjustFmChannelAttenuation
units.summary: Ignore this change during a fade or in PSG mode. Otherwise add the stream operand to channel attenuation and join the FM instrument/volume write helper.

units.name: SetAudioDurationScale
units.summary: Copy the stream operand into the independent audio duration-scale field.

units.name: SetPsgNoiseModeAndPitchCoupling
units.summary: OR the operand with E0 and write the PSG noise latch. The low mode bits decide whether channel flag 6 is cleared or set; in the coupled path also release suppression on DEAE. Preserve the encoded OR-FC/increment test rather than treating every noise register value alike.

units.name: AudioCommandReturnStub
units.summary: Immediate return for this command path.

units.name: SelectAlternateAudioPitchInstrumentMode
units.summary: Operand one saves transpose/instrument fields, sets channel flag 5 and enters the alternate mode. In FM mode it forces transpose 12 and instrument flags 53 before refreshing hardware state. Other operands restore the saved values and clear flag 5; PSG mode does not perform the FM instrument stores.

units.name: ReleaseSharedAudioChannelByRegister
units.summary: Use the encoded channel-register comparisons to release the appropriate shared record. Restore PSG noise/tone ownership, cached noise latch or FM volume state as required; one active-DF2E branch jumps to the stack-sensitive stop helper. The final path sets the selected gate byte to 1F, the driver silence state.

units.name: RestoreFmSharedInstrumentNibblePair
units.summary: Select the DF35 instrument/attenuation bytes and join their common FM register restore helper.

units.name: UpdatePsgNoiseChannelFrame
units.summary: Advance elapsed ticks and service the slot-specific noise stream when duration expires. Suppression and gate bit 4 block hardware output. Otherwise resolve the selected attenuation envelope, combine its value with F0 and write the PSG noise volume latch. This reader is selected by channel-slot contract, not register E0 alone.

units.name: DispatchNoiseReaderCommand
units.summary: Supply CPU 8B44 as the command return continuation and join the existing audio command dispatcher at 87BE.

units.name: SelectNoiseEventLatchAndEnvelope
units.summary: Decode the noise-event bitmask in priority order. Select envelope/instrument kind 1..4, attenuation 2..4 and noise latch E4/E5/E6; bit 2 can reduce the attenuation by two. Cache the latch at DE08 and suppress the hardware write when channel flag 2 is set. A mask with no selected event disables the envelope and emits FF unless suppressed.

units.name: AudioEnvelopeReturnStub
units.summary: Immediate return after the pitch/envelope container helpers.

units.name: PlayOneBitPsgSample
units.summary: Read exactly 0548 bytes from bank-6 CPU ACA2, emitting eight MSB-first bits per byte as PSG volume 90/9F with the encoded six-count delay. Quiet existing audio, program the initial PSG latch and temporarily write zero to F2. After all 1352 bytes restore driver mode to F2, restore active PSG noise state when needed and join the common audio continuation. No sample rate or original recording identity is inferred.

units.name: CheckSelectedBonusShotSlot
units.summary: Return immediately if the selected shot type is zero; otherwise continue with its presentation/hitbox check.

units.name: FadeAndReleaseSharedAudioVoices
units.summary: Inspect the DF0E/DF2E voice states, stop their PSG/FM outputs as required and clear their active/suppression state. Initialize a 12-step fade with 18-tick delay, then quiet the selected FM registers in FM mode. The adjacent restoration entries return shared hardware channels to their music/effect owners and join the common driver continuation.

units.name: RestoreSharedNoiseAndFmChannel
units.summary: Clear the DF2E state, release suppression in DECE/DEAE and restore FM register 35 from the stored instrument/attenuation nibbles. Reset request priority and adjacent voice state before restoring the remaining shared channels.

units.name: ReleaseSharedPsgToneChannels
units.summary: Clear request priority and shared voice state, release suppression on three records and emit the stored three-byte PSG sequence around the FM register helper calls. If DF2E remains active, release its suppression and restore the PSG noise latch or FM register 35 according to driver mode.

units.name: BeginAudioGateRelease
units.summary: Set channel flag bit 0, back up DE by one and return to the stream service. The following gate handler owns release progression.

units.name: SetAudioFlagFiveFromOperand
units.summary: Set channel flag 5 only for operand one; all other values clear it.

units.name: SetAudioFlagThreeFromOperand
units.summary: Set channel flag 3 only for operand one; all other values clear it.

units.name: SkipModeSpecificAudioOperand
units.summary: In PSG mode enter the existing alternate reader continuation; in FM mode advance DE over the mode-specific byte and return.

units.name: ReadPsgNoiseStreamEvent
units.summary: Read the channel stream pointer and distinguish commands E0+, ordinary note/duration data and noise-selection events 80+. Preserve duration reuse through SoundLastDuration and enter the established command/stream continuations. This is the specialized noise/drum reader retained by the finite stream analysis.

units.name: UpdatePsgToneChannelFrame
units.summary: Advance elapsed ticks, service stream expiry and update the signed fractional pitch delta with high-byte carry/borrow. Apply suppression, gate and release tests before the attenuation envelope and PSG volume write. For active pitched notes, resolve the pitch envelope, honor coupling flag 6 and emit the period as the encoded PSG latch/data pair. Register E0 is remapped to C0 for the coupled tone write; slot-specific reader selection remains separate.

units.name: EvaluatePsgAttenuationEnvelope
units.summary: Index the selected envelope with channel field 12. Positive values advance the cursor, add channel attenuation and clamp on bit 4 to 0F. Marker 82 restarts at zero; 81 sets gate FF and unwinds the helper return; 80 unwinds to the common pitch continuation. Other high markers read an explicit new cursor byte and retry. These stack exits are part of the envelope control format.

units.name: ResumePsgAttenuationEnvelope
units.summary: Resume the attenuation envelope at its existing field-12 cursor; the preceding entry first replaces that cursor with A.

units.name: InitializeOpeningPresentation
units.summary: Initialize mode zero once, map bank 2 into CPU8000, expand the common graphic and upload 35 two-plane tiles plus a 4x10 tile rectangle. Start a 240-tick delay and palette transition; after the shared completion test, advance to mode81.

units.name: SetVdpAddressFromDE
units.summary: Write DE to the VDP control port. The following rectangle writer consumes B rows of C tile bytes, pairs each with the saved attribute A, and advances the VRAM row by64 bytes. Callers must provide valid port timing and nonzero counts.

units.name: WriteTileRectangleWithAttribute
units.summary: Save attribute A and emit B rows of C tile IDs from HL. DE is the VDP destination; each row starts64 VRAM bytes after the previous row.

units.name: UploadTwoPlaneTiles
units.summary: Upload B tiles from HL after setting VDP address DE. Each tile has eight rows: emit its two source plane bytes, then two zero planes. Stack exchanges supply the VDP port delays; counts must be nonzero.

units.name: UploadTwoPlaneTileRows
units.summary: Emit D rows using two source bytes and two zero planes per row; XOR A establishes the cleared planes.

units.name: InitializeAttractPlayback
units.summary: Initialize mode two once, load the bank2 presentation, alternate between two descriptors in bank4, copy the chosen stage plus five playback-state bytes, and start gameplay with session bit4 set. Completed playback advances to mode6; otherwise enter the existing gameplay path.

units.name: ResetFromAttractPlayback
units.summary: Silence/reset the bank6 sound service, restore the bank2 graphic and display state, clear work RAM C040..DDFF, then select mode81 with no delay.

units.name: MultiplyUnsigned16By16
units.summary: Multiply BC by the original DE with sixteen shift/add steps. DE:HL receives the unsigned32-bit product; A is the loop counter. The carry from each low-word addition increments the high word. Caller and natural reachability remain unknown.

units.name: SampleControllerToAuxiliaryShadow
units.summary: Use the established controller reader and store its result in C603. No caller is established for this wrapper.

units.name: UploadBytesThroughPlaneMask
units.summary: Save the four-bit plane mask A, set VDP address HL, and read BC bytes from DE. Emit each byte four times, replacing disabled planes with zero; alternate registers hold the port and mask loop. Requires valid counts, source bank and VDP access; no caller established.

units.name: ExpandTwoStridedRamPlanes
units.summary: Expand two terminated tagged streams from HL into alternating bytes at DE and DE+1. Each packet uses low7 bits as count: high bit selects advancing literal bytes, otherwise repeat one byte; zero tag returns. The inner writer advances destination by2. Valid stream/count/buffer are caller preconditions; caller unknown.

units.name: ExpandStridedRamPacket
units.summary: Read the next tagged packet; a zero tag ends this plane. Preserve the high-bit literal flag while writing its low7-bit count at destination stride2.

units.name: ReadVramAndWriteBitReversedBytes
units.summary: Read BC VRAM bytes through the established reader into D800 scratch, then reverse each byte bitwise and write it at the original VDP address. Interrupt guards protect address/output accesses. Requires valid count and scratch capacity; no caller established.

units.name: FinishLatchedPlayerDirections
units.summary: Pushed-return continuation for ApplyLatchedPlayerDirections. Protected motion waits for the primary timer, then chooses animation06/16 from facing; ordinary motion selects primary type1. All paths return to the original caller.

units.name: MoveObjectAgainstCameraDelta
units.summary: Negate the signed camera delta and pass it to the common movement service; return A=0. Caller and natural reachability remain unknown.

units.name: ApplyCollisionCategoryResponse
units.summary: With bank2 mapped, category18 uses the special actor-exclusion path. Other categories preserve flags0/6, merge the category response, select a HUD/reward adjustment and continue at the meter service. IX is the acting object and IY the contacted object; selector production is not fully known.

units.name: FilterSpecialActorCollision
units.summary: For actor type16, reject target categories0 and19..1C; eligible categories enter the existing hit response. Other actor types enter the general category service. Bank2 and valid IX/IY records are required.

units.name: ScanSevenCollisionSlots
units.summary: Probe seven slot pointers with the established overlap helper. On a hit, combine the facing-dependent response bits into the contacted object. At progression2+ apply the filtered category response; earlier progression uses the general service. Bank2 must remain mapped.

units.name: ApplyContactDamageOrDefeat
units.summary: Reject non-damage categories, consult the category response count, then either enter temporary recoil type6F or the defeat path. Recoil saves the original type, selects direction flags, sets timer30 and Y velocityFE00. Defeat selects a reward, requests soundA4 and type66, marks stage slots for categories6/17, then advances the bounded ten-event counter when its session flags allow. Requires bank2 and valid IX/IY records.

units.name: AddPackedBcdScoreReward
units.summary: Skip scoring during attract playback. Index a four-byte reward record and add its three packed-BCD bytes into C042..C040 with decimal carry; mark score display dirty. Compare against the next three-byte threshold; on crossing it, add decimal10000 to that threshold and saturating-increment the life/reward counter. Bank2 and valid reward selector are required.

units.name: UpdateBestPackedBcdScore
units.summary: Compare current three-byte packed-BCD score C040 with best score C013. Copy all three bytes only when current score is greater. Direct fixed-window entry explicitly maps bank2; no natural execution claim.

units.name: CompareThreeByteValues
units.summary: Lexicographically compare three bytes at DE with HL, most significant first. Return carry set when DE is less than or equal to HL, clear when DE is greater; restore both pointers for the caller.

units.name: AddAndClampHudMeter
units.summary: Add A to meter C06D, clamp the unsigned result to12hex, then fall through the established HUD update service with A=0. Enter only with bank2 mapped; sum is computed modulo256 before the clamp.

units.name: ClampHudMeterPair
units.summary: Clamp values18 or above to18 and mirror the clamped value to the preceding meter byte; branch to the shared display update.

units.name: ClearExhaustedHudMeter
units.summary: On the exhausted-meter path, clear its byte and set the pending update flag in C06B before joining the shared continuation.

units.name: QueueGlobalEffect
units.summary: Maintain a four-entry FIFO of effect IDs and parallel pairs of parameter words. A nonfull queue appends; a full queue shifts the oldest item out and inserts the new one using its four-byte descriptor. Set the pending flag after insertion. Bank2 and valid effect selector are required; selector zero aliases preceding opcode bytes and must not be normalized.

units.name: RemoveOldestGlobalEffect
units.summary: Shift effect IDs and both word arrays toward the head, zero the vacated tail, clear the active flag and decrement queue count. Clear pending only when the queue becomes empty.

units.name: ReleaseSoundAttenuationGate
units.summary: Bank6 channel helper: rewind DE one token, inspect the low attenuation nibble and return for zero. Otherwise convert the release state to40/80 flags in channel field8 and tail-call the established attenuation writer. IX is a32-byte channel; actual caller unknown.

units.name: AdvanceSoundChannelLoopCounter
units.summary: Use channel-local byte28 as a loop counter. Zero initializes from token-1 and skips two bytes; an active counter decrements and chooses one/two-byte cursor advance. Bank6 IX/DE stream contract applies; actual caller unknown.

units.name: ResumeNoiseStreamAfterCommand
units.summary: Pushed command continuation from bank6 noise dispatcher: advance DE past the command and resume the established noise reader. Preserve this slot-specific reader contract.

units.name: DispatchPlayerActionButtons
units.summary: Dispatch player action and direction buttons in priority order; separate from the encounter offset cycle.

units.name: PlayerButtonMaskTable
units.summary: Six button masks consumed by the player-button dispatcher, ending at the independent mode-zero entry.

units.name: OpeningPaletteRequest
units.summary: Counted palette-transition request consumed by mode-zero initialization.

units.name: AttractInputPairsAndInitialState
units.summary: Thirteen paired attract-input values followed by five initial playback-state bytes. The finite input reader and following routine bound the storage.

units.name: AttractPagePointers
units.summary: Three little-endian pointers selected by the attract-page sequence.

units.name: AttractPlaybackDescriptors
units.summary: Two attract-playback descriptors selected alternately. Each chooses a stage plus five bytes copied to playback state; bank4 contains the referenced controller streams.

units.name: StageGraphicsPaletteResourcePointers
units.summary: Three19-word little-endian pointer arrays: stage graphics, raw32-byte palettes, and stage resources. StageIndex0..18 supplies the finite domain. Graphics/palettes use bank5; raw palettes are distinct from counted palette requests.

units.name: DisplayClearFillValues
units.summary: CPU0C02 word0900 and CPU0C04 byteE0 consumed by FillVramWord/FillVramByte to reset display name/sprite tables.

units.name: DefaultPaletteEntries
units.summary: Sixteen default palette bytes copied to palette RAM with an explicit16-byte block transfer.

units.name: PlayerOscillationDisplacements
units.summary: Twenty-four signed little-endian Y displacement words. The oscillation phase wraps at24 and doubles its index before adding the word to primary8.8 Y.

units.name: PlayerBounceVelocityProfiles
units.summary: Three six-byte signed velocity profiles: Y, right-facing X, left-facing X. The bounce counter is clamped to0..2 before multiplying by6.

units.name: ProjectileSlotCounts
units.summary: Five slot-count bytes indexed by projectile allocation; these are scalar counts, not pointers.

units.name: BonusObjectSlotPointers
units.summary: Nine little-endian RAM object/queue-slot pointers. Values designate RAM records and must not be followed as ROM code.

units.name: EncounterRandomYPositions
units.summary: Four Y positions selected by a masked refresh-register value.

units.name: QuantizedHeadingMagnitudeRecords
units.summary: Heading data: nine four-byte quantized magnitude pairs, sixteen aligned little-endian pointers, four orientation flags, four transforms, sixteen paired magnitudes and five six-byte encounter payloads. Consumers establish the representation; original generator/rounding is unknown.

units.name: EncounterAnimatedStripPointersAndTiles
units.summary: Three little-endian strip pointers and three58-byte animation strips, selected modulo3. Following repeated tile/index storage feeds scrolling; its exact internal partition is unresolved.

units.name: EncounterTargetYPositions

units.name: EncounterEffectOffsetPairs
units.summary: Eight Y/X byte-offset pairs for SpawnEncounterOffsetEffectCycle. Its selector wraps at8 and doubles the index; the consumer handles position extension carries.

units.name: StageMarkerRecords
units.summary: Twenty four-byte marker records: animation, X, Y and a following value. Nineteen stages plus the explicit alternate index select the records.

units.name: OpeningTwoPlaneTilesAndRectangle

units.name: CollisionTileIdListWithRecordAlias
